doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: The evils of the road: water and diet
summary: Travel upsets the stomach and eating out constantly hurts health.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You also learn a few things traveling. Don’t drink the water. You know you to go San Francisco, and you change water, and all of a sudden you’re feeling strange. You go down to Los Angeles, you drink that water, oh this is weird, it upsets your whole system.
So the evils of the road.

Well that and even food, you know eating out all the time. If you have to eat in restaurants all the time, it’s not as good as what you probably would have if you were eating at home you know. It’s all right to eat out occasionally but when you have to eat out every day, breakfast, and dinner, you have to be careful about your diet if you want to feel good. limited. So that’s another thing that’s important though when you’re traveling, because otherwise your health — you know if you don’t feel good, you can’t work well and do well.
